title: Veridian Tech — Edge SDK / Proxy Integration Discovery
summary: Intro discovery focused on integration patterns: SDK usage, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy placement, rate limiting/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer leaning towards a hybrid approach; strict data residency and audit requirements. Agreed to run a short bench and provide TCO scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
next_steps: Alex Rivera - Send Dedicated vs Private TCO + pilot pricing - due 2027-04-12
Samir Patel - Share sample LangChain connector snippet and benchmark config - due 2027-04-14
Jules Ortega - Provide expected QPS and percentiles on 2 week traffic sample - due 2027-04-13
Priya Kapoor - Confirm compliance checklist items and any on-prem constraints - due 2027-04-15
action_items: Alex Rivera - Compile security pack (SOC2 audit, KMS integration docs) - 2027-04-12
Jordan Lee - Prep small perf benchmark runbook and share link to results sheet - 2027-04-14
Customer (Jules) - Export sample traffic histogram (p95/latency, request size) - 2027-04-13
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Maya Chen (Veridian CTO): Maya here. Jules, Priya, Liam on.
[00:08] Alex Rivera: Great. Samir and Jordan from my side, SE and solutions. We put a short agenda in the invite—integrations, proxy/gateway patterns, and security constraints. Does that look right?
[00:18] Jules Ortega (Customer): Yup that's right. We're primarily worried about where to put Redwood in our stack; cloud-hosted looks easiest but we have some data residency and some PII rules.
[00:27] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Totally. quick question: are you looking at Redwood Hosted first for an MVP or do you already have a mandate for dedicated/private?
[00:35] Liam Ford (Customer): We prefer hosted for dev/prod parity but security folk may push for Dedicated or Private for certain hosts. It's per-team; some teams could be allowed to use Hosted, others will need VPC.
[00:45] Priya Kapoor (SecOps): Right—also we need KMS integration and audit logs for every inference request, retention 7 years for logs. we also need to ensure tokens aren't stored in third-party infra.
[00:56] Jordan Lee (Redwood SE): Understood. Redwood Private can run in your VPC or on-prem, and our control plane can be isolated. For KMS we integrate with AWS KMS and HSMs; we can discuss bring-your-own-key.
[01:07] Maya: How intrusive is the integration? We already run an API gateway + service mesh.
[01:11] Samir: Two common patterns: 1) call Redwood via a central gateway (we provide SDKs for python/node) or 2) sidecar/proxy per service that does request shaping, KV cache, and batching. Both work—sidecar reduces cross-network hops but needs per-node runtime.
[01:26] Jules: Are there examples for LangChain or LlamaIndex? we're using both for different teams.
[01:31] Alex: Yes; we have LangChain connectors and a LlamaIndex adapter in our repo. i'll share a snippet. Samir, do you want to call out the connector differences?
[01:38] Samir: Sure, there are two things—auth and streaming. Our SDK has direct client bindings that LangChain can call. For LlamaIndex, we recommend the simple LLMPredictor wrapper. There was some earlier transcription mix-up in our docs calling it "LantiChain" but it's LangChain. Also note streaming early outputs may need websocket or chunked-http and some of our Hosted endpoints support streaming.
[01:54] Maya: latency is a big one for us. our customer-facing product needs 200-300ms p95. can Redwood hit that on Hosted?
[02:02] Jordan: depends on model and sequence length. For small instruction models we see <100ms p50 and ~200-300ms p95 in our benchmarks on dedicated capacity. Hosted has multi-tenant noise—so we recommend Dedicated or pinned instances for strict p95 SLOs. We'll share benchmark sheet.
[02:21] Liam: and cost? if we go Dedicated what's the cost delta vs Hosted?
[02:25] Alex: Dedicated is predictable (monthly commit) and typically about X2 on fixed infra but you get better tail latency. We'll send a TCO calc—Hosted per-token vs Dedicated amortized infra.
[02:36] Priya: rate limits — we need per-tenant quotas and burst controls. some of our clients have spikes.
[02:41] Samir: Redwood supports per-key quotas and dynamic rate limiting. You can configure quotas at API-key or route level and set burst windows. Also we've got token-level metering so you can bill per-token.
[02:54] Jules: What about observability—how much telemetry do you expose? we need traces correlated with our request ids, and token-level cost breakdowns.
[03:01] Jordan: We emit structured logs, request traces, and token cost breakdown per request. You can hook into Datadog/Lightstep via our tracing headers, and we have an events webhook for each inference result. The console also has per-route dashboards with token usage and latency histograms.
[03:18] Maya: Can we get a sample alerting rule? like if p95 crosses threshold or model regresses on quality.
[03:24] Samir: Yep—we recommend alerts on p50/p95 and a quality regression hook that ties to evals. We'll include examples in the runbook.
[03:32] Liam: A practical integration question: do you want us to put Redwood behind our existing Kong gateway or run a sidecar? pros/cons?
[03:39] Alex: If you want to centralize auth and rate limiting in Kong, it makes sense to call Redwood from the gateway as a downstream. For per-instance caching (prefix/KV cache) sidecar is better. Gateway approach is simpler to start.
[03:51] Jules: Are there SDK examples for Node microservices to do streaming and retry logic?
[03:56] Jordan: Yes, Node SDK includes chunked streaming example and a small retry/backoff helper. We'll share code gist.
[04:03] Priya: Regarding compliance, you mentioned SOC2 and audit logs. do you also support SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[04:09] Samir: Yes, SSO with SAML/OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, and role based access controls. For Private installs we can enable customer-managed identity provider.
[04:18] Maya: Any gotchas with KV cache and multi-tenant data? we don't want cache bleeding between tenants.
[04:23] Samir: We namespace caches by tenant id and have strong isolation; on Dedicated you can also opt for per-tenant cache instances. We'll include that in the docs.
[04:33] Alex: Quick note—on batching: automatic batching can reduce tokens per second cost but can add latency. you can tune batching window, or disable it for low-latency endpoints.
[04:44] Jules: How do we handle fallbacks during capacity spikes? we need graceful degradation.
[04:48] Jordan: Redwood routing supports fallback policies—route to a cheaper/compatible model or to a stalled response with retry recommendation. For critical paths you can pin a model on Dedicated to avoid fallback.
[05:00] Maya: Ok. can you run a small perf run against our sample traffic? We'll share a week of anonymized traffic.
[05:05] Alex: yes we can run a bench. Jordan will run it with three configurations: Hosted default, Dedicated pooled, and Private in your VPC (if you want). We'll provide a results sheet with p50/p95/cost.
[05:16] Priya: One more Q: encryption in transit and at rest—do you support customer-managed keys for stored prompts/kv?
[05:22] Samir: Yes, CMKs for stored artifacts. For ephemeral KV cache we can avoid persistent storage in Hosted; for Private you can use your own KMS.
[05:29] Liam: Do you have guardrails for prompt injection or sensitive data scrubbing?
[05:33] Jordan: We have some built-in redaction rules and can plug in custom scrubbing functions pre-inference. We'll share the sample code.
[05:41] Alex: (brief pause) ok time check—we have about 40 minutes left so let's go deeper on the integration flow and then recap next steps.
[05:48] Samir: I'll describe an example flow: client request -> Kong gateway (auth, rate-limit) -> Redwood gateway endpoint (or sidecar) -> Redwood runtime (batching, kv cache) -> model -> response with trace-id injected. We recommend injecting your request-id in X-Request-Id header so traces correlate.
[06:08] Jules: Could you show the snippet for LangChain usage?
[06:11] Jordan: (shares link in chat) gist: https://redwood.co/gists/langchain-veridian-example . Example shows LangChain llm wrapper plus streaming handler. Caveat: there was an older example that used an outdated param name, so use the latest gist.
[06:26] Maya: streaming + websocket: do you have an inbound websocket proxy?
[06:29] Samir: Hosted supports chunked HTTP streaming; for websocket you can either proxy through your gateway to our streaming endpoint or use Dedicated which has more configurable streaming transports. We'll add recommended Nginx/Envoy configs.
[06:43] Liam: For quotas—can we set daily and per-minute limits and get webhook alerts when near limit?
[06:48] Alex: Yes. Quotas, burst windows, and alert webhooks are all supported. we'll include example policy JSON in the runbook.
[06:58] Priya: On data residency—some of our EU customers require that data stays in eu-west-1. Can you pin region?
[07:04] Samir: Yes, region pinning is supported. Hosted has EU regions; Dedicated gives you region exclusive capacity; Private you run in your VPC/region. We'll note the supported regions in the security pack.
[07:16] Jules: request—please include a sample policy for per-tenant billing using token usage export to our billing system.
[07:22] Jordan: We export token-level usage via daily CSV or streaming events. We can add an example lambda that ingests events into your billing tables.
[07:32] Maya: Are there customers doing exactly what we want? any references in regulated space?
[07:36] Alex: We have a couple of financial customers on Dedicated and one health care partner on Private. We'll share anonymized case studies.
[07:45] Liam: about SLA—what uptime and latency SLAs come with Dedicated?
[07:49] Samir: Dedicated includes an SLA for availability and latency tails; exact numbers depend on contract tier. We'll include baseline SLA language in the proposal.
[07:58] Maya: Cool, I'm going to hand over to Priya for compliance specifics.
[08:01] Priya: Thanks. Quick clarification—audit logs must be immutable and retained 7 years. also need full export for eDiscovery. Is that doable?
[08:09] Jordan: Yes, logs can be exported to your S3 with immutability flags for Private; for Hosted we offer export and can work on retention, though for immutability we normally recommend Dedicated/Private. We'll include details.
[08:21] Alex: All right, let's capture explicit next steps. we'll run bench against sample traffic and share pricing/TCO. Jordan will share code samples and the LangChain gist. Alex will share security pack. Customer to share anonymized traffic and compliance checklist.
[08:36] Maya: That sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:39] Alex: Thanks all. we'll follow up with materials and schedule a technical deep-dive once the bench is complete.
[08:45] (end of recording)
